source_review.notes: Reviewed the original O'Neil-Cheng-Gawlick-O'Neil LSM paper, current Google LevelDB implementation notes, current RocksDB overview and leveled/universal/general compaction documentation, and current Apache Cassandra storage-engine and compaction documentation. All eight final destinations returned HTTP 200. Current product policies are examples and remain distinct from the abstract LSM correctness contract.

evidence: Checked memtable/run base M, ratio T, data size N, level count L, consulted runs R, internal entry tuple, snapshot visibility, and manifest generation.
Checked sequence, transaction order, wall clock, tombstone, TTL, merge operand, user key, and internal key are not conflated.
Checked read/write/space amplification examples require explicit physical/logical scope and inclusion policy.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Level count is presented as an approximate policy model, not an exact amplification formula.

evidence: Recomputed nine input records across three sources and five unique keys after newest-sequence resolution.
Recomputed a is found in one source as A5, b in three as B1, and e@7 deletion masks E2.
Recomputed service-debt example: 200 MiB/s generated versus 150 MiB/s sustainable creates at least 50 MiB/s growing debt before further amplification.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The finite source consultation counts rely on the model's newest-to-oldest nonoverlapping sequence epochs.

evidence: Verified newest snapshot-visible internal entry determines value/deletion for each user key across all candidate sources.
Verified complete k-way merge plus version-retention predicate preserves every supported snapshot's logical map.
Verified tombstone elision is unsound when any unselected older value or snapshot/repair horizon can make that value observable again.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No universal amplification constant is inferred from leveled or tiered policy labels.

evidence: Reviewed empty/duplicate keys, sequence ties/wrap, batches/aborts, many versions, tombstones, TTL, merge operands, snapshots, range endpoints, and corrupt filter/index metadata.

Reviewed partial/torn WAL, memtable freeze races, file/footer/sync/manifest crash boundaries, replay duplication, orphan outputs, missing files, CURRENT/manifest corruption, and delayed input deletion.
Reviewed incomplete overlap, stale replica/repair resurrection, backup/change-stream retention, L0 explosion, debt/stalls, ENOSPC/temp space, tenant starvation, and benchmark non-steady state.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: The executable model excludes files, transactions, snapshots other than latest, concurrency, recovery, distributed state, and safe garbage collection.

evidence: Each finite source is checked sorted by user key and compaction chooses the maximum sequence for each key.
Compacted keys are checked as the unique sorted key set; exact latest a and deletion e establish version resolution.
Exact output checks input/unique counts, version-retaining compacted records, visible map, run consultations, tombstone suppression, source ordering, and aggregate validity.
invariant_checking.notes: The point-read shortcut is explicitly qualified by ordered source epochs and is not a general overlapping-file algorithm.

evidence: Reviewed acknowledged-write recovery from WAL durability through memtable freeze, verified run, durable manifest install, and safe WAL release across every crash prefix.
Reviewed point/range merge from complete candidate enumeration through internal ordering, snapshot visibility, tombstone/merge resolution, output order, and file-version pinning.
Reviewed compaction from complete overlap closure through retention horizons, output validation/sync, atomic manifest edit, reader-safe retirement, and orphan/input reconciliation.
proof_review.notes: The proof structures state implementation obligations and do not constitute a mechanized or product-specific verification.

evidence: Write/recovery, read/merge, and compaction proof structures are separately labeled.
Bloom filters, checksums, file metadata, source ordering, current vendor behavior, and finite merge execution retain their exact scope.
Tombstone age, successful file write, high burst throughput, or clean shutdown is never generalized into correctness.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Correctness, recoverability, distributed anti-resurrection, resource stability, and performance are distinct evidence surfaces.

evidence: The standard-library Python model passed exact twelve-line stdout, empty stderr, and zero exit status under the repository verifier.
It reproduced five newest versions from nine inputs, four visible values, one/three-source reads, tombstone suppression, ordering, and valid=True.
All eight external destinations returned HTTP 200 and repository-local structure/link checks passed.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No WAL, memtable implementation, SSTable, filter, manifest, file/device I/O, snapshot transaction, compaction job, crash recovery, distributed repair, fuzzing, or performance test was executed.

conceptual_review.notes: The chapter presents the LSM as a versioned pipeline with conservation, publication, retention, and queue-stability invariants rather than merely a memtable plus files, and connects tombstone safety to complete overlap and external horizons.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed WAL/ack ordering, freeze/flush/manifest/WAL release, candidate reads, filters, leveled/tiered/FIFO assumptions, compaction selection/publication, reader pinning, tombstone/TTL/repair horizons, backpressure, recovery, telemetry, and steady-state testing.

pedagogical_review.notes: The one-page review establishes lifecycle and invariants; the finite model makes version/tombstone resolution explicit; ten examples cover write recovery, snapshots, overlap, debt, and space; five exercises provide full read/write/compaction designs and incident audit answers.

limitations: Internal authoring, primary/maintainer-source, mathematical, bounded executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic, O'Neil, Cheng, Gawlick, LevelDB, RocksDB, Cassandra, database, distributed-systems, storage-engine, reliability, security, performance, or independent practitioner review is claimed. The chapter and model prove neither WAL/memtable durability, SSTable/filter/manifest correctness, snapshots/transactions, compaction implementation, tombstone collection, distributed repair, recovery, resource stability, production amplification, certification, nor deployment fitness.
